original_question: Let S be a finite subset of P^N, let a(S,1) be the least degree of a hypersurface containing S, and let e(S) be the Waldschmidt constant lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m. Is it always true that (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N <= e(S)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1 ("Asymptotic effectivity"), Conjecture 2.1.2: Chudnovsky’s conjectured lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant e(S). The immediately following Problem 2.1.3 gives the paper’s nearby equality-case discussion. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact inequality the paper asks about, uses the paper’s notation a(S,1) and e(S), and places the problem in the correct ambient space P^N. In substance, it is already very close to Conjecture 2.1.2. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The paper assumes S={p1,...,pr} is a finite set of distinct points in projective space P^N over an algebraically closed ground field k of arbitrary characteristic. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

To define e(S), one needs a(S,m) for every integer m>=1, not only a(S,1). The paper defines e(S)=lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m and recalls that this limit exists. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The paper’s official definition is a(S,m)=min{d : h^0(X,L(d,m))>0}, where X is the blow-up of P^N at S and L(d,m)=dH-m(E1+...+Er). In stand-alone form, this should be unpacked as: a(S,m) is the least degree d of a hypersurface vanishing to order at least m at every point of S. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The quantifiers should be explicit: the question is whether the inequality holds for every integer N>=1 and every such finite set S. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

If you want the paper-faithful nearby scope, the next question in the paper is not another bound but the equality-case classification in Problem 2.1.3; your draft does not mention that, which is fine, but it helps locate the exact target. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let N>=1, and let S={p1,...,pr} be a finite set of distinct points in P^N_k. For each integer m>=1, define a(S,m) to be the least integer d such that there exists a degree-d hypersurface in P^N_k vanishing to order at least m at every point of S, and set e(S)=lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m. Must one always have (a(S,1)+N-1)/N <= e(S)?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the asymptotic-effectivity discussion in Section 2.1, not a later or broader neighboring problem. The paper first fixes distinct points S={p1,...,pr} in P^N over an algebraically closed field k of arbitrary characteristic, introduces the blow-up X->P^N and the divisor L(d,m)=dH-m(E1+...+Er), and defines e(S)=lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m with a(S,m)=min{d : h^0(X,L(d,m))>0}. Immediately after recalling the weaker Waldschmidt-Skoda bound a(S,1)/N <= e(S), it states Conjecture 2.1.2, namely (a(S,1)+N-1)/N <= e(S). The next item, Problem 2.1.3, discusses when equality might force S to lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration, so that is nearby context but not the main statement your draft is asking about. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
